browser-use/cdp:
The sandbox browser speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
Point Playwright or Puppeteer at the browser's CDP endpoint and your agent drives the **same** browser the live viewer shows - same tabs, same logins, same page.

The CDP endpoint is a WebSocket on `api.miosa.ai`:

```text
wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/browser/cdp
```

It is control only. A view-only share token is refused here.

## Get the endpoint

`POST /browser` starts the browser and returns `cdp_url` and `stream_auth`:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

## Authenticate the CDP socket

The socket takes the same credentials as the stream:

- `?token=<stream_auth>` - the token returned by `POST` (1 hour). Simplest for an agent.
- `Authorization: Bearer <msk_* API key>` - API keys need the `sandboxes:exec` scope; a browser can reach anything the sandbox can, so the scope is deliberate.

## Playwright

> **Note: Already-open context**
>
> The browser is already running with a page. Use the existing context and page instead of launching a new browser, so you act on the session the viewer sees.

**Python**

```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

cdp_url = f"{browser['cdp_url']}?token={browser['stream_auth']}"

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser_conn = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp_url)
    context = browser_conn.contexts[0]
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else context.new_page()

    page.goto("https://example.com")
    print(page.title())

    browser_conn.close()   # detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

**JavaScript**

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const cdpUrl = `${browser.cdp_url}?token=${browser.stream_auth}`

const browserConn = await chromium.connectOverCDP(cdpUrl)
const context = browserConn.contexts()[0]
const page = context.pages()[0] ?? (await context.newPage())

await page.goto("https://example.com")
console.log(await page.title())

await browserConn.close()   // detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

You can pass the token as a header instead of a query parameter when your client supports it, for example Playwright's `connect_over_cdp(cdp_url, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + api_key})`.

## Puppeteer

**JavaScript**

```javascript
import puppeteer from "puppeteer"

const browser = await puppeteer.connect({
  browserWSEndpoint: `${browserInfo.cdp_url}?token=${browserInfo.stream_auth}`,
})

const [page] = await browser.pages()
await page.goto("https://example.com")
console.log(await page.title())

await browser.disconnect()   // detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

> **Caution: Disconnect, do not kill**
>
> `browser.close()` in Playwright and `browser.disconnect()` in Puppeteer detach the agent.
> They do not stop the sandbox browser, so a viewer stays connected.
> To stop the browser and free its memory, `DELETE /browser` - see [Limits](/docs/browser-use/limits).

## One browser, two drivers

Because the viewer and the agent share one browser:

- A person can open the live viewer while an agent is running and watch the agent work.
- If a person takes control, the agent's next action lands on the same page.
- Cookies and logins persist across both, and across pause and resume of the sandbox.

Keep the agent and the human from acting at the same instant by taking control only when the automation is idle.

## Close codes

If the socket closes before it is ready, the close code says why:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `4001` | Unauthorized |
| `4003` | Forbidden (the key lacks `sandboxes:exec`) |
| `4004` | Sandbox not found |
| `4009` | Sandbox not running |
| `4012` | Browser not started - call `POST /browser` first |
| `4013` | Tenant stream limit reached |
| `4014` | Share link expired or revoked |
| `1011` | Upstream failure |

browser-use/how-it-works:
## What you get

- **A live browser**: Start it in any running sandbox and watch the page render in real time on the Sandbox page.
- **Take control**: A viewer can take control and use the browser directly, or share a revocable view-only link.
- **Agent access over CDP**: Playwright and Puppeteer connect over CDP and drive the same browser the viewer is watching.
- **Sandbox-priced**: It runs inside the sandbox you already have, so it bills as plain sandbox usage.

## How it fits together

- **Start.** Ask the sandbox to start its browser. It starts lazily on the first request, stays up across pause and resume, and stops when you stop it.
- **Watch and drive.** The Sandbox page shows the live browser. A viewer can take control; a view-only link can watch but never drive.
- **Automate.** Playwright or Puppeteer connect to the live browser over CDP and act on the same session a person sees.

Because the viewer and the automation share one browser, a person can open the page mid-run, watch, and take control without losing cookies, logins, or page state.

## The three viewers of one browser

| Surface | Who | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Live viewer on the Sandbox page | The signed-in owner | Watch the browser, take control |
| View-only share link | Anyone with the link | Watch only; cannot drive the browser |
| CDP endpoint | An agent (Playwright, Puppeteer) | Drive the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol |

> **Caution: View-only means view-only**
>
> A view-only share link cannot type, click, or navigate. Input is rejected inside the browser process in the sandbox, not just hidden in the UI.

> **Note: Everything goes through api.miosa.ai**
>
> Both sockets - the live-view stream and the CDP endpoint - are on `api.miosa.ai`, with normal API authentication.
> Nothing is exposed on the sandbox's own host or on a template port.

## See also

- **Drive it over CDP**: Playwright and Puppeteer connecting to the same browser.
  [Open](/docs/browser-use/cdp)
- **Limits, billing, security**: Minimum size, lifecycle, billing, and how access is enforced.
  [Open](/docs/browser-use/limits)
browser-use/integrations:
Any client that speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol can drive a sandbox browser.
Only clients verified end to end on MIOSA are listed here; more will be added as they are proven.

## Compatibility

Each client below was run against a live sandbox browser: connect, navigate, click, type, screenshot, and confirm a live viewer sees the same page.

| Client | Language | Version | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Playwright | JavaScript | 1.64.0 | **Tested** |
| Playwright | Python | 1.63.0 | **Tested** |
| Puppeteer | JavaScript | 25.13.0 | **Tested** |
| Raw CDP | Node (no library) | Node 24 | **Tested** |
| Stagehand | JavaScript | 3.7.3 | **Tested** |
| browser-use | Python | 0.13.11 | **Tested** |
| Computer use (screenshot + actions) | Any HTTP client | - | **Tested** |

## Connect

Every CDP client connects to the same endpoint on `api.miosa.ai`:

```text
wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/browser/cdp
```

`POST /browser` starts the browser and returns `cdp_url` and `stream_auth`.
Authenticate the socket one of two ways:

- **Token in the URL.** Append the `stream_auth` token as `?token=`:

  ```text
  wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/browser/cdp?token=<stream_auth>
  ```

- **Authorization header.** `Authorization: Bearer <msk_* API key>` (the key needs the `sandboxes:exec` scope), for clients that can set headers on the WebSocket.

Both go through `api.miosa.ai`; nothing is exposed on the sandbox's own host.
The endpoint is control only: a view-only share token is refused here.

`POST /browser` also returns `cdp_ws_url` and `cdp_http_url`, which carry the token in the path for clients that cannot set headers or append a query string.
`cdp_http_url` answers `/json/version`, `/json/list`, `/json/new`, and `/json/protocol`, and rewrites every advertised `webSocketDebuggerUrl` to itself, so clients that follow discovery stay authenticated.

> **Note: Reuse the open context**
>
> The browser is already running with a page. Use the existing context and page instead of launching a new browser, so you act on the session the live viewer shows.

## Client examples

**Playwright (JavaScript)**

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const cdpUrl = `${browser.cdp_url}?token=${browser.stream_auth}`

const browserConn = await chromium.connectOverCDP(cdpUrl)
const context = browserConn.contexts()[0]
const page = context.pages()[0] ?? (await context.newPage())

await page.goto("https://example.com")
console.log(await page.title())
await page.screenshot({ path: "page.png" })

await browserConn.close()   // detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

Or authenticate with a header, avoiding the token in the URL:

```javascript
const browserConn = await chromium.connectOverCDP(browser.cdp_url, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY}` },
})
```

**Playwright (Python)**

```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

cdp_url = f"{browser['cdp_url']}?token={browser['stream_auth']}"

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser_conn = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp_url)
    context = browser_conn.contexts[0]
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else context.new_page()

    page.goto("https://example.com")
    print(page.title())
    page.screenshot(path="page.png")

    browser_conn.close()   # detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

**Puppeteer**

```javascript
import puppeteer from "puppeteer"

const browser = await puppeteer.connect({
  browserWSEndpoint: `${browserInfo.cdp_url}?token=${browserInfo.stream_auth}`,
})

const [page] = await browser.pages()
await page.goto("https://example.com")
console.log(await page.title())

await browser.disconnect()   // detaches; it does not stop the sandbox browser
```

Puppeteer can also discover the socket for you: pass `browserURL: cdp_http_url`, and Puppeteer reads `/json/version` and follows the rewritten `webSocketDebuggerUrl`.

**Raw CDP (WebSocket)**

```javascript
// Plain WebSocket, no client library.
const url = `${browser.cdp_url}?token=${browser.stream_auth}`

const ws = new WebSocket(url)
const pending = new Map()
let nextId = 1

ws.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  const message = JSON.parse(event.data)
  pending.get(message.id)?.(message)
  pending.delete(message.id)
})

const send = (method, params = {}) =>
  new Promise((resolve) => {
    const id = nextId++
    pending.set(id, resolve)
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }))
  })

await new Promise((resolve) => ws.addEventListener("open", resolve))
console.log((await send("Browser.getVersion")).result.product)

// Page-level work: discover a page target through /json/list,
// then open a second socket to its page-level URL.
const list = await (await fetch(`${browser.cdp_http_url}/json/list`)).json()
console.log(list[0].webSocketDebuggerUrl)
```

**Stagehand 3.x**

```javascript
import { Stagehand } from "@browserbasehq/stagehand"

const stagehand = new Stagehand({
  env: "LOCAL",
  localBrowserLaunchOptions: {
    cdpUrl: `${browser.cdp_url}?token=${browser.stream_auth}`,
  },
})

await stagehand.init()
const page = (await stagehand.context.pages())[0]
await page.goto("https://example.com")
console.log(await page.title())
```

**browser-use**

```python
import asyncio
from browser_use import Browser

async def main():
    # `browser` is the POST /browser response: { "cdp_url": ..., "stream_auth": ... }
    cdp_url = f"{browser['cdp_url']}?token={browser['stream_auth']}"

    agent = Browser(cdp_url=cdp_url, is_local=True)
    await agent.start()
    page = await agent.get_current_page()
    await page.goto("https://example.com")
    print(await page.get_title())
    # browser-use evaluates with the function form:
    print(await page.evaluate("(...a) => document.title"))
    await agent.stop()

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Computer use (no CDP)**

```javascript
// OpenAI/Anthropic computer-use style loop: screenshots plus coordinate actions.
// No CDP in the client at all.
const base = `https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/${sandboxId}/browser`
const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` }

// A screenshot of the current page
const shot = await fetch(`${base}/screenshot?format=png`, { headers })

// Navigate, type, and click by coordinate
await fetch(`${base}/actions`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { ...headers, "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    actions: [
      { type: "navigate", url: "https://example.com" },
      { type: "wait", ms: 600 },
      { type: "type", text: "miosa" },
      { type: "click", x: 140, y: 270 },
    ],
  }),
})
```

Action types are `click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, `move`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key` (for example `"ctrl+a"` or `"Enter"`), `navigate`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, and `wait`.
`GET /browser/screenshot` takes `format=png|jpeg`, `encoding=base64`, and `tab=ID`.

## Stagehand 4.x

Stagehand 4.x is not supported: it requires pipe-only CDP.
Use Stagehand 3.x.

> **Caution: Detach, do not kill**
>
> `browser.close()` in Playwright and `browser.disconnect()` in Puppeteer detach your driver. They do not stop the sandbox browser, so a viewer stays connected.
> To stop the browser and free its memory, `DELETE /browser` - see [Limits](/docs/browser-use/limits).

## See also

- [Drive it over CDP](/docs/browser-use/cdp) - the endpoint, auth, and close codes in full.
- [Live viewer](/docs/browser-use/live-viewer) - watch and take control of the same browser.
browser-use/limits:
## Availability

Browser use is available on every running sandbox, on any template.
One exception today: a SOMA sandbox ships Docker and Chromium but not the virtual display the live viewer renders, so the live viewer is not available on SOMA yet.
The browser starts lazily on the first `POST /browser`, so sandboxes that never use it pay nothing and boot as fast as before.

The sandbox image must include a Chromium-family browser and Node.
Every MIOSA sandbox image ships them; a custom image that removed them returns `501 BROWSER_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

No template publish is needed to use the browser: the daemon ships with the control plane and is written into the sandbox on start, on every launchable template.

## Size

A real Chromium needs room. `small` (2 vCPU, 4 GB) or larger is recommended for a comfortable browser.

| Size | vCPU | RAM | Browser use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` | 1 | 2 GB | Tight; a single light page at most |
| `small` | 2 | 4 GB | **Recommended minimum** |
| `medium` | 4 | 8 GB | Comfortable |
| `large` | 8 | 16 GB | Heavy pages and parallel tabs |

## Lifecycle

| Action | Effect on the browser |
|---|---|
| `POST /browser` | Starts the browser lazily (idempotent) |
| Pause sandbox | Browser state is preserved; the session survives resume |
| Resume sandbox | The same browser comes back, with its tabs and logins |
| `DELETE /browser` | Stops the browser and frees its memory; the sandbox keeps running |
| Destroy sandbox | Removes everything, including browser state |

Pause and resume keep the browser; stopping the browser is what releases its memory.

## Saved website sign-ins

The platform stores a person's saved website sign-ins so the sandbox browser can fill them without the agent ever seeing the password.
`GET /api/v1/signins` lists them, `PUT /api/v1/signins/{site}` saves one, and `DELETE /api/v1/signins/{site}` removes one.
Send `workspace_id`; a request without it answers `422 WORKSPACE_REQUIRED`.
Responses are masked: they carry a username preview and `last_used_at`, never the password.
`POST /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/browser/signin` with `{"site": "..."}` fills the saved sign-in into the open tab, only on your own running sandbox and only on an HTTPS page of that site.

The browser is also a process inside the sandbox, so if the sandbox is restarted the browser must be started again. `GET /browser` reports the current state (`running`, `stopped`, `unavailable`, or `sandbox_not_running`) without starting anything.

## Billing

Browser use bills as **plain sandbox usage**.
There is no separate browser line item: while the sandbox is running, you pay the sandbox rate you already pay for that size, and the browser runs inside it.
Stopping the browser frees memory but does not by itself stop the sandbox.

## Security

- Nothing is exposed publicly. Both sockets - the live-view stream and the CDP endpoint - go through `api.miosa.ai` with normal API authentication, never through the sandbox's own host.
- The control plane connects to the browser daemon on the sandbox's loopback only, and hands it a 60-second token each time. Callers never see that token.
- An **API key on a socket needs `sandboxes:exec`**, because a browser can reach anything the sandbox can.
- Share tokens are **view-only**. Their input is refused inside the sandbox's browser process, not merely hidden in the UI.
- Share links are **revocable**: revoke one link by its `share_id`, or revoke every share and CDP link at once. Revoking bumps the browser's share epoch, so an outstanding link stops working immediately.
- Live-view and CDP sockets share a per-tenant stream limit; exceeding it closes the socket with `4013`.

> **Caution: Never expose the API key**
>
> Mint viewer and CDP access on your backend.
> Send only the short-lived `stream_auth` token or a share link to the browser or the agent.
> Never ship a MIOSA API key to the frontend.

browser-use/live-viewer:
The live viewer renders the sandbox browser in a page you can watch.
It needs the sandbox's virtual display (`Xvfb :99`), which ships in the sandbox image, and which a SOMA sandbox does not have yet.
It lives on the Sandbox page in the MIOSA console, and the same protocol serves any client you build.

The viewer is a WebSocket at `wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/browser/stream`: JPEG frames and JSON events come down, JSON input goes up.
It goes through `api.miosa.ai`, never the sandbox's own host.

## Three ways to open it

| Surface | How | Capability |
|---|---|---|
| Sandbox page | Open the sandbox, then its browser panel | Take control |
| Stream URL | `stream_url` from the browser API, with `stream_auth` | Take control |
| View-only share link | Minted for someone else | Watch only |

## Authenticate the stream

Two ways, both on `api.miosa.ai`:

- `Authorization: Bearer <msk_* API key | session JWT>`, or
- `?token=<stream_auth>` for clients that cannot set headers (the `stream_auth` value from `POST`).

API keys used here need the `sandboxes:exec` scope.
A viewer that only watches can pass `?mode=view`, which reaches the view-only listener in the sandbox.

## Take control

A viewer opened on the Sandbox page, or with a control-mode stream, can take control: click, type, scroll, and navigate the live page.
Input goes straight to the browser process, so the page the agent is driving is the page you are steering.

## Share a view-only link

Mint a share link to let someone watch without touching the browser.
No MIOSA login is required to use it.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser/share?ttl_seconds=600" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "data": {
    "mode": "view",
    "share_token": "bs1.1783000000.0.9f3c...",
    "expires_at": "2026-10-10T13:00:00Z",
    "stream_url": "wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/sbx_01j9x/browser/stream"
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mode` | Always `view`. |
| `share_token` | The view-only token; pass it as `?share=<share_token>` on `stream_url`. |
| `expires_at` | When the link stops working. |
| `stream_url` | The stream WebSocket the link connects to. |

`ttl_seconds` is optional: it defaults to `3600` and must be between `60` and `604800` (7 days).
Out of range is `400 INVALID_TTL`.

The share link opens the same stream as a view-only viewer:

```text
wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser/stream?share=$SHARE_TOKEN
```

A view-only link is **revocable**: revoking it stops every outstanding link for that browser immediately.

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser/share \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

```json
{ "data": { "revoked": true, "epoch": 1 } }
```

Revocation bumps the sandbox's share `epoch`; every token minted at an earlier epoch is rejected from then on.

> **Caution: A view-only link cannot drive**
>
> View-only is enforced inside the sandbox's browser process, not in the page. A view-only viewer receives frames; its input is refused on the machine, so it can never type, click, or navigate - whatever mode it asks for.

## Full screen

The viewer has a full-screen control that expands the browser to the whole screen for closer inspection or a kiosk-style display.
Toggle it off to return to the embedded frame.

browser-use/quickstart:
Browser use runs inside a sandbox, on every template, with no extra setup.
You create a sandbox as usual, then start its browser.

The browser starts lazily on the first `POST`. Sandboxes that never use a browser pay nothing, and sandbox boot stays as fast as it is today.

## 1. Start a sandbox

Any sandbox works, on any template. Nothing about the browser is chosen at create time.
The live viewer needs the sandbox's virtual display, which a SOMA sandbox does not have yet.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "template_id": "miosa-sandbox", "size": "small" }'
```

Wait until the sandbox `state` is `running`.

## 2. Start the browser

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

The response carries everything you need:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "state": "running",
    "epoch": 0,
    "viewport": { "width": 1280, "height": 720 },
    "stream_url": "wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/sbx_01j9x/browser/stream",
    "cdp_url": "wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/sbx_01j9x/browser/cdp",
    "stream_auth": "miosa_stream_...",
    "stream_auth_expires_at": 1783000000
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `running` when the browser is up. |
| `epoch` | Share-link epoch. Bumping it revokes every outstanding share link. |
| `viewport` | Browser viewport, `1280` by `720`. |
| `stream_url` | WebSocket for the live view (`wss://api.miosa.ai/...`). |
| `cdp_url` | WebSocket Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint for agents. |
| `stream_auth` | A short-lived token for the viewer or CDP socket. |
| `stream_auth_expires_at` | Unix seconds when `stream_auth` expires (1 hour). |

`POST` is idempotent: calling it again on a running browser returns the same endpoints without restarting it.

> **Note: Scope**
>
> `GET` needs the `sandboxes:read` scope.
> `POST` and `DELETE` need `sandboxes:write`.
> The WebSocket endpoints need `sandboxes:exec` when you authenticate with an API key.

## 3. Open the viewer

In the MIOSA console, open the sandbox and use its browser panel.
To open the viewer yourself, connect to `stream_url` and authenticate.

```bash
# The viewer protocol is a WebSocket: JPEG frames and JSON events down, JSON input up.
# Pass the token as a query parameter...
wss://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser/stream?token=$STREAM_AUTH
# ...or as a header: Authorization: Bearer $STREAM_AUTH
```

From there a viewer can **take control** of the browser or share a **view-only link**.
See [Live viewer](/docs/browser-use/live-viewer).

## 4. Let an agent drive it

The browser a person is watching is the same browser an agent connects to over CDP.
Connect to `cdp_url` with Playwright or Puppeteer - see [Drive it over CDP](/docs/browser-use/cdp).

## 5. Check the state without starting it

`GET` only reports state; it never starts the browser.

```bash
curl https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "data": { "state": "running", "epoch": 0, "viewport": { "width": 1280, "height": 720 } }
}
```

For a sandbox that is not running, `state` is `sandbox_not_running` and no guest is touched:

```json
{ "data": { "state": "sandbox_not_running", "epoch": 0 } }
```

## 6. Stop the browser

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "data": { "state": "stopped", "epoch": 0, "viewport": { "width": 1280, "height": 720 } }
}
```

Stopping the browser frees its memory while the sandbox keeps running.
The browser survives **pause and resume** of the sandbox; stopping it is what releases the memory.

## Errors

| Status | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `INVALID_ID` | The sandbox id is not a UUID |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | Unknown sandbox, or one owned by another tenant |
| `401`/`403` | - | Missing or insufficient credentials |
| `409` | `SANDBOX_NOT_RUNNING` | The sandbox must be running to start or stop the browser |
| `501` | `BROWSER_NOT_AVAILABLE` | The sandbox image has no Chromium or Node |
| `502` | `BROWSER_START_FAILED` | The browser daemon did not come up in time |

`501` names a template that ships the browser prerequisites: the sandbox image includes Chromium and Node.
